Derivatives of the Expected Information Under an Explicit Method

Source: R/dexpected_method.R
dexpected_by_method.Rd

Returns the derivative of order m of the matrix that an ExpectMethod defines, with respect to the parameters, on the parameter scale or the link scale. It is the route of distrib_dexpected_hessian(), distrib_d2expected_hessian(), distrib_d3expected_hessian() and distrib_d4expected_hessian() when method is an object.

Usage

dexpected_by_method(distrib, y, theta, scale, m, method)

Arguments

distrib

A univariate distribution.

y

A numeric vector of observations.

theta

A named list of parameters, aligned.

scale

"parameter" or "link".

m

The derivative order, 1 to 4.

method

An object inheriting from ExpectMethod.

Value

A named list keyed as dexpected_names(), d2expected_names(), d3expected_names() or d4expected_names().

Details

For expect_integrate() and expect_mc() the matrix is \(E_{ab}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_\theta[f_{ab}]\) and each derivative moves the density as well as the integrand, so that the integrand of the derivative along \(c\) is \(\partial_c f + f\,\ell_c\). For expect_opg() the matrix is \(f_{ab}\) evaluated at the observations, the data do not move, and the derivative is the Leibniz derivative of \(f_{ab}\) alone: \(-(\ell_{ac}\ell_b + \ell_a\ell_{bc})\) at order 1 and \(-(\ell_{acd}\ell_b + \ell_{ac}\ell_{bd} + \ell_{ad}\ell_{bc} + \ell_a\ell_{bcd})\) at order 2. The integrand \(f_{ab}\) is \(\ell_{ab}\) for identity = "hessian" and \(-\ell_a\ell_b\) for identity = "score"; expect_opg() uses the second.

The derivative of order m of \(f_{ab}\) needs observed derivatives of order up to m + 1 for the score identity and m + 2 for the Hessian identity. The package provides five orders, so the Hessian identity at m = 4 signals an error that names identity = "score".

On the link scale the parameter-scale derivatives of every order up to m are computed by the same method and carried across by dexpected_link_higher().
